c.tagline: Botswana's dusty tourism capital and the gateway to the Okavango Delta.

taxi.fareNote: There is no ride-hailing app in Maun. Blue combi minibuses run fixed routes for a flat few pula, while private 'special' taxis are unmetered - agree the fare before setting off. Most visitors rely on lodge transfers and rental 4x4s.

emergency.note: 999 reaches police, 997 the ambulance and 998 fire. Letsholathebe II Memorial Hospital is the main hospital, and safari lodges arrange air-ambulance evacuation from remote Delta camps.

english.label: Easy to get by in English

avoid.reason: Petty theft from vehicles and campsites occurs; avoid walking alone along unlit roads after dark.

hood_desc: The commercial heart of Maun around the Old Mall and the airport, packed with banks, supermarkets, safari operators and the small Nhabe Museum; the practical, walkable base most visitors use to stock up and arrange trips into the Delta.

A riverside ward southeast of town along the Thamalakane and toward the Boro, lined with lodges, campsites and mokoro (dugout canoe) stations; a relaxed, green base close to the water and the Delta poling routes.

The lodge strip northeast of town on the Shorobe road, where thatched riverside lodges and tree camps overlook the Thamalakane; a scenic, quiet base for sundowners and scenic-flight departures over the Delta.
A residential ward north of the centre near Letsholathebe II Memorial Hospital, with guesthouses and the riverside Sedia hotel; calm and local, an easy drive from the shops and airport.
A traditional local ward across the Thamalakane from the centre, with homes, small eateries and everyday Maun life; the least touristy base, good for travelers wanting an authentic, low-key stay.

water.note: Town supply is treated but variable and sometimes brackish; most visitors stick to bottled or filtered.

transit.pay: Combi fares are a flat few pula paid in cash to the driver; 'special' taxi fares are negotiated before the ride. There is no fare card, pass or app system.
transit.hours: Combis run roughly 6am-7pm and thin out after dark; arrange a taxi or lodge transfer at night.
transit.note: Maun has no rail, metro or formal city bus; locals get around on blue combi minibuses running fixed routes and on shared 'special' taxis, while most visitors rely on lodge transfers, rental 4x4s and taxis. The town is spread out along the river, so walking only really covers the central mall area.

bus: Intercity coaches to Francistown, Gaborone and Kasane/Chobe

transit.m: Taxi or lodge transfer to central Maun (~5 min)
Light-aircraft charter transfer into the Okavango Delta camps

tip.r: Tipping is customary in the safari/lodge sector - roughly $10-20/day for safari guides and mokoro polers; ~10% at restaurants is appreciated.

food.name: Seswaa
food.desc: Botswana's national dish: beef or goat simmered for hours in a three-legged pot then pounded into salty shreds, served over maize or sorghum porridge.

places.name: Choice Take Away and Restaurant
places.note: Busy local canteen where seswaa with pap is the everyday lunch plate.

places.name: Kwagancinci
places.note: Sit-down spot built around Botswana home cooking rather than safari menus.

places.name: Maun Lodge
places.note: Reliable hotel dining room that keeps seswaa on the local-dishes section.

food.name: Braai
food.desc: Open-fire barbecue of beef steak, ribs and coiled boerewors sausage, cooked over wood coals and eaten with pap and chakalaka relish.

places.name: The Old Bridge Backpackers
places.note: Long-running riverside camp with a famous grill and firepit atmosphere.

places.name: Sedia Riverside Hotel
places.note: Poolside braai nights and hearty grills; a Maun institution for decades.

places.name: Choice Take Away and Restaurant
places.note: Cheap grilled meat plates for people who want the local version, not the lodge one.

food.name: Morogo
food.desc: Wild leafy greens gathered after the rains, stewed down with onion and tomato and sometimes finished with groundnuts; the standard vegetable side.

places.name: Choice Take Away and Restaurant
places.note: Morogo appears daily in the steam-tray line beside the meat.

places.name: Kwagancinci
places.note: Serves morogo as part of a full Setswana plate rather than as an afterthought.

food.name: Bogobe and pap
food.desc: Stiff sorghum or maize porridge that anchors nearly every meal; the sour lerotse melon version, bogobe jwa lerotse, is the local favourite.

places.name: Choice Take Away and Restaurant
places.note: Ask for bogobe rather than rice to eat the way Batswana actually do.

places.name: Maun Lodge
places.note: Buffet lunches usually include both maize pap and sorghum bogobe.

food.name: Game meat
food.desc: Kudu, ostrich, springbok and impala grilled as steaks or turned into dry spiced biltong; leaner and gamier than beef, and unmistakably Botswanan.

places.name: Sedia Riverside Hotel
places.note: Game steaks show up regularly on the specials board before safari departures.

places.name: The Old Bridge Backpackers
places.note: Grill menu often runs kudu or ostrich; a good pre-mokoro dinner.

places.name: Maun Lodge
places.note: Convenient in-town option for a first taste of Botswana game meat.

food.name: Grilled Okavango bream
food.desc: Freshwater tilapia and tigerfish from the delta channels, scored and grilled whole over coals with lemon, chilli and salt.

places.name: The Old Bridge Backpackers
places.note: Riverside deck a few steps from the water where the fish comes from.

places.name: Sedia Riverside Hotel
places.note: Fish from the Thamalakane and delta appears whenever the catch allows.

food.name: Traditional sorghum beer
food.desc: Bojalwa jwa Setswana, the thick, sour, low-alcohol home-brew of fermented sorghum; the commercial Chibuku version comes in a carton you shake first.

places.name: Bars around Maun Main Mall
places.note: Local bars and bottle stores keep Chibuku cold; ask staff before wandering in.

places.name: Sedia Riverside Hotel bar
places.note: Easier introduction for visitors, with staff happy to explain the brew.

food.name: Botswana lager
food.desc: Locally brewed St Louis and Kgalagadi lagers, drunk ice-cold at sundown; the standard reward after a day in the delta.

places.name: The Old Bridge Backpackers
places.note: Classic sundowner bar over the river, full of guides and mokoro polers.

places.name: Maun Lodge
places.note: Central terrace bar for a cold one without leaving town.

landmarks: Mokoro excursions on the Boro River
Poled silently through lily-covered channels in a traditional dugout canoe, the quintessential delta experience departs from villages just outside Maun.
Thamalakane River
Maun's lifeline riverfront, where fish eagles cry over sunset boat cruises and lodges line banks grazed by donkeys and hippos.
Chief's Island
The delta's largest landmass within Moremi, famed for exceptional big-game density and reachable on fly-in or boat safaris from Maun.
Nhabe Museum
A modest museum in a 1939 colonial building presenting Ngamiland's San, Batawana and Herero heritage plus local contemporary art.
Maun Educational Park
A small riverside reserve on the edge of town where impala, kudu and zebra wander walking trails, a gentle safari primer.
Old Matlapaneng Bridge
A rickety 1960s wood-and-rail causeway across the Thamalakane, a nostalgic relic of Maun's dusty frontier-town days.
Lake Ngami
The fickle Kalahari lake that stunned explorer David Livingstone in 1849, drawing huge flocks of pelicans and flamingos in flood years.
Motsana Cultural Centre
A community arts hub in town selling local crafts and occasionally staging traditional theater, a low-key window into Batawana culture.
Maun Environmental Education Centre
A riverside center on the Thamalakane's eastern bank teaching visitors and schoolchildren about the Okavango's wildlife and wetland ecology.
Boro-bonche Ostrich Farm
A working ostrich farm a short drive from town where visitors can get close to the birds and learn about the breeding operation.

train.note: No railway reaches Maun. Botswana Railways' single main line runs north-south from Lobatse through Gaborone to Francistown and the Zimbabwean border at Ramokgwebana, leaving the whole north-west of the country unserved, and in any case all Botswana Railways passenger services, including the BR Express, have been suspended (https://www.botswanarailways.co.bw/). Travellers arriving by train from South Africa or Zimbabwe therefore have to finish the journey to Maun by coach or air.

bus.note: No international coaches serve Maun directly. Long-distance buses and combis run to Francistown (~7 hr), Gaborone (~10-12 hr) and Kasane for Chobe (~7 hr, via Nata). Most travelers arrive by air, and onward Delta travel is by light aircraft or 4x4.

ferry.note: Maun sits on the Thamalakane River at the southern edge of the Okavango Delta, but there are no scheduled ferries or public boat services; delta transfers are by chartered motorboat or poled mokoro arranged through a lodge or tour operator, and the Kazungula ferry to Zambia far to the north-east was replaced by a road bridge in 2021.

half.name: Okavango Delta (mokoro & scenic flight)
half.blurb: The vast inland delta on Maun's doorstep, explored by dugout mokoro, motorboat or a small-plane scenic flight over its maze of channels, lagoons and islands teeming with elephant, hippo and birdlife.

half.name: Boro / Nxaraga mokoro station
half.blurb: The nearest poling stations on the Delta's edge, where guides pole travelers through the reeds for a half-day on the water and short walks on the islands.

full.name: Moremi Game Reserve
full.blurb: The reserve on the eastern Delta (~2-3 hr by 4x4), one of Africa's richest wildlife areas with lion, leopard, wild dog and elephant across floodplains and mopane woodland.

full.name: Makgadikgadi & Nxai Pans
full.blurb: Vast salt pans ~3-4 hr east, seasonal home to zebra migrations, meerkats, baobabs and desert-adapted wildlife.

full.name: Khwai Community Area
full.blurb: A community-run wildlife concession bordering Moremi, known for excellent big-cat and elephant sightings and mobile camping.
